en: (What the hell? Where'd all these kids come from?)
You all gotta go home and wait till Christmas to get your presents!
I can't wait that long!
Pwease can I have it now, Santa?
Lemme go get my friends! They want presents, too!
No! Don't tell any other kids I'm here!
I just posted online where Santa is. Everyone's coming.
Ya posted what?
Santa, how come you don't have my present!?
Hey, I was here first!
(Gah... I gotta just make a break for it!)
It was pointless... Wearin' the Santa getup brought kids swarmin'. Couldn't do a thing with them around.
Oh, that's too bad. I guess there's nothing we can do...
Hey, I'll give it one more go. Let me use the Santa outfit again, if ya don't mind.
Wow, you're no quitter! Thank you very much for trying again. All of us Santas have our ho-ho-hopes in you!
Yeah, yeah...
Oh, oh! What about me?
Santa! I want my present!
Yeah... don't think there's anythin' we can do.
(All right. Gotta hit the town again and find those Santa hunters.)
Um, do you think you're going to look for the Santa hunters again? Or should all of us retail Santas just accept our very un-jolly fates?
I'll give it one more go. Let me use the Santa outfit again, if ya don't mind.
Wow, you don't give up! Thank you very much for trying so hard.
I wish you luck.
So you are %s. I hear you've been on a bit of a rampage around here.
Let's see how good you are.
Hmm. Seems you can hold your own.
Next time we meet, I won't hold anything back.
Hmph. That's the best you can do? Pathetic.
You'd better train harder. Next time we meet, you'll be in for a lot more pain.
(Damn, he's got some skills, all right. Who is he?)
(That was quite the show. Who is this guy?)
(Ain't fought anyone that strong in a while. Wonder who he is.)
(Ow... That guy was something else. Is this how everyone fights here in Kamurocho?)
Hi, I'm Haruka.
----Change (null)----.
You wanna play a game of mahjong, man? Gotta have 25,000 points on you. You can buy 'em over at the desk.
Hey, buddy. You want to play with us? We're just okay⑬not too great, not too bad.
Yeah, I'll play.
That's what I like to hear! Let's go, then.
No, I'll pass.
Shame... Let me know if you change your mind.
Hey, buddy. You want to play with us? We're pretty damn good, though.
Lookin' for a game? We got room for ya. All ya need is 25,000 points of mahjong sticks. Get 'em at the front desk.
Hey, buddy. You want to play with us? We got a chair free if you want to join.
Hey, bud. Wanna play after all? You'll need 25,000 points of mahjong sticks. They're at the front desk.
Hey, guy. You want to play with us? We're regulars here, and we're pretty tough. How about it?
Something come up? Well, it's been fun. Come back again sometime!
That was fun. Let's gather around the table again sometime.
Hey, buddy. You want to play with us? Not to brag or anything, but we play reasonably well.
Hey, guy. You want to play with us? I have to warn you, we're pretty hot. Are you up for it?
Hey, buddy, don't I know you from Orchid Palace Mahjong? We're a man short. How about you join us for a game?
Oh, wait a second. You got no mahjong sticks. Want to buy 25,000 points so you can play?
All right. I'll join you.
That's the spirit. Let's tickle us some ivory.
Whoops, guess ya don't have the cash right now. We'll play some other time, then, yeah?
Hey, buddy! How about joining me in a game?
Nishina-san still hasn't come back.
We should probably accept that Nishina-san and Kihachi are both... you know...
No! Nishina-san would never screw up that bad, and neither would Kihachi. They're alive, I know it!
Somethin' the matter, Sakurai-han?
Did you hear? One of our hunters, Kihachi, never came down from the mountain.
And Nishina-san went to find him, but now they're both missing!
Anyone aside from Nishina-han go out searchin'?
No... because...
Lemme guess. People're scared of Yama-oroshi?
Well. They're right to be scared.
What about Nishina-han's missus? She know about it?
Of course. But she acts like nothing's wrong 'cause she's one hell of a strong woman.
Any idea where the hunter Kihachi was going?
No, but I'm sure he wouldn't have gone far. He's not that dumb.
Well, that's somethin'.
And hopefully you're not dumb, either... Don't get any ideas about going up that mountain.
All we can do now is wait. We shouldn't let the mountain swallow up anybody else.
(There's wisdom there, but...)
(In any case, think I'll go see Nishina's wife.)
(Maybe later.)
Nishina-san was worrying himself into a frenzy...
We should avoid that, so we don't do anything brash. They'll be okay, I'm sure of it...
My poor husband...
(Nishina-san's helped me out before. Can't sit by doin' squat while she suffers.)
(I'll talk to Okudera-han, and then I'm gonna go find her man.)
"White Darkness" was added.
Who is that...?
You all right, man? You Kihachi-han?
Ah, it's... it's you. What are you doing here?
Put that outta your mind for now. Ya seen Nishina-han anywhere? He came out here lookin' for ya.
Uh, no, I haven't seen him.
Okay. First things first, you need rescuin'. Can ya walk?
I don't think so. I'm not hurt that bad. It's just... I'm so cold...
(He's really weak. Better give him some food.)
I'll bring ya some food; ya just gotta hang on a little longer. Be tough, you can do it!
I'll try...
Here, eat this. It'll perk ya up. And don't fall asleep! That'll kill ya.
Mm... that really helps. Thank you. Thank you so much.
Don't worry 'bout it. You're in need.
(Damn, it's turned into a blizzard now. Can't see a thing.)
This is it... This is how I die...
Hey, don't give up!
(Can't go anywhere with the weather like this... I'll get lost.)
(Sakurai-han was right... I was stupid to come up here.)
Hey, we're gonna ride out this blizzard together, ya got that? I'll be right here. Just hang on, Kihachi.
Nishina-han's out here somewhere, lookin' for ya. We gotta put our faith in him, now!
(Blizzard's still ragin' like an angry wife with a fryin' pan. Damn, my arms and legs feel heavy...)
(This... could be the end.)
(Can't... stay awake...)
You... you came back for me.
'Course I did. Now hang on just a little longer!
You're better already?
I'm sorry. I only caused yer husband more trouble.
No, you did your best to help. You are so kind-hearted... maybe too much so, haha!
Please, listen to us when we say that the mountain is a frightful, dangerous place.
Yeah, I learned that lesson the hard way.
Oh, hey! Saejima-san, right?
You and Nishina-san saved my life! Thank you.
Nah, Nishina-han alone saved ya. And he saved me, too. I was jus' a burden in the end.
But you gave me food, and hope! Here, take this.
Go on, take it. Please, it would make me happy!
Oh, all right. 'Preciate it.
You got <Color:8>Leghold Trap<Color:Default>.
We got lucky this time. Be careful out there.
Yeah. I will.
Now where was I...? Ah, it doesn't matter! I'm just glad you're back, Saejima-san!
You were gone a long time, and we were getting worried that you were lost or something!
Nope. But I got news...
Are you serious!? You found Yama-oroshi's den?
We haven't confirmed it yet. But we're pretty damn sure.
Where is it?

en: Quite a ways into the wilderness. It ain't even on any of the village maps.
Where's Okudera-san, now?
He went home to cook supper. Didn't seem to wanna talk about it, actually.
Really? Hm, that's kind of strange. You'd think he'd be excited. Let's go see him.
What the hell? Where'd he go?
I knew something was up. The old salt's gone to the mountain.
No way⑬the sun's close to settin'. He wouldn't be that reckless. I mean, shit, I hope not.
Saejima, don't you remember? When you first met Okudera, it was nighttime, yes?
He don't care what time it is. Not when it comes to that fucking bear.
Don't worry. I'll go get him and bring him home.
You won't make it!
Huh? Nishina.
Okudera is fast⑬the fastest in the village. And yes, I'm including the hunters.

He also knows the mountain better than anyone.
You'll never catch him.
Then what do ya suggest we do?
Well, can you drive a snowmobile?
Huh? Ya got one?
Yeah, we do. So can you?
I can, but I ain't an expert...
Come with me.
Okudera-han! Okudera-han!
Sae... Saejima?
Geez, ya can barely talk! Did Yama-oroshi get ya!?
Ugh... urrrgh.
I'm takin' ya back to the village right now! Hold on! Doncha die on me. Ya got that!?
No... Saejima, I'm not...
Don't talk. Gotta save yer strength! We'll talk later.
Don't you see? I'm... I'm not... who you think. I'm not... Okudera.
Hey! Stay with me! Can ya hear me? Okudera-han!
Hi, Saejima-san.
Uh, yer husband told me ta come round.
Okay. He's with Sakurai-san in the shed.
I never told you this, but my husband, and Sakurai-san, and all the village's hunters... They've all tried very hard to protect Okudera-san.
Uh-huh. Sure seems that way.
You know the stories of how, even when others stay off the mountain, Okudera-san will march up there into the bitter cold and freezing wind?
Yeah, I know.
It's not true.
When Okudera-san goes out, some of the other hunters always watch him at a distance, to make sure nothing happens to him.
What? Were they doin' that for me, too?
(That must be how Sakurai-han knew exactly where Okudera-han would be.)
It's the least the people of this village can do.  That's how much we owe Okudera-san.
If it hadn't been for him nine years ago, our entire way of life would have been lost to the ages.
For goodness' sake, what are ya talkin' about?
My husband will tell you the rest.
You came.
For a minute. Ya got one minute.
I wanted to show you this...
What the!?
Relax, it's not alive. It's stuffed.
Why is it here?
About a dozen years ago, the village had a booming side business. This is all that's left of it.
Side business?
At the time, the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties was up for revision. These revisions were going to deeply affect us as a community.
They banned all hunting except that which was part of the livelihood and subsistence of traditional people like us.
But even with the exception, it was still a total ban on recreational hunting. For everyone.
In the months before the new law was to take effect, our mountain was flooded with trophy hunters.
Most of them were commissioned by fur dealers and taxidermists, who were hoping to nab big game before the law took effect.
But the mountain's very unforgiving in winter, as you know well by now. So all these hunters kept getting lost and dying.
Eventually, the dealers offered the jobs to us.
And ya sold out.
The money was good. For poor villagers like us, it was like nothing we'd ever dreamed of. Our lives seemed transformed by riches.
Day after day, we just kept hunting.
Until we finally tipped the balance of nature. On our own mountain.
Wait, is that why Yama-oroshi showed up?
Yes. The bears had never attacked us before.
But we had put them in a situation where they could only survive by stalking and killing humans.
Desperate animals will do anything. Just like people.
We think the man whose name was recorded by authorities as "Sato" was one of those hunters who came here during that time to make money. As you know, he went missing...
Possibly because he was chasing Yama-oroshi, who of course was the most prized pelt of all.
Sure, he went for the jackpot.
Yeah. But Okudera⑬our friend⑬he wasn't motivated by the almighty dollar. He risked his life to protect the village from Yama-oroshi.
And after it was all over, he didn't even boast about it. He just continued to live quietly as a hunter. In truth... he made us all remember how a hunter should live.
Okudera-san is truer to the spirit of the hunt than any of us native villagers.
Even now, he fights Yama-oroshi alone for all our sakes.
He is trying to free us from the terror we've lived with for the past nine years. I know it.
Nishina-han...
I saw it!
That voice came from the village! Let's go!
Ya all right?
Calm down! You saw what?
Yama-oroshi! Yama-oroshi was just outside!
Are you sure!?
I'm sorry, I don't have time to convince you! I'm going home and locking up!
I never expected him to come so close to our village.
Nishina-han.
I'll go.
Please don't joke.
Not jokin'... Look, there's something I been keepin' from all of ya. I'm like Okudera-han. I broke outta prison, too.
No! You're an escaped convict!?
We could report you.
'Cept now I wanna help ya, and it ain't outta some hope that ya won't turn me in.
